_comment: NInfer serving Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 on :8080 — the apples-to-apples match for `qwen3.8-27b-vllm`, which is what the descent benchmark actually runs. MEASURED 2026-08-17, not inferred: unlike the 3.6 artifact, this template IS effort-capable — none/low/medium/xhigh are accepted and OpenAI's `high` is rejected with reasoning_effort_not_supported, which is the same low/medium/xhigh rung set core's `vllm_effort` dialect was written against. The dialect must nevertheless be `openai`, because NInfer takes reasoning_effort as a TOP-LEVEL field and rejects unknown non-null chat_template_kwargs — which is exactly what vllm_effort sends, so it would 400 every request. Consequence worth knowing: core's `high` maps to the literal string `high` on the openai dialect and therefore cannot reach this template's top rung at all. Reaching `xhigh` would need a third generic mapper in core (top-level reasoning_effort, xhigh rung) — a protocol-level mapper with no vendor name in it. Serve with: --spec mtp --draft-tokens 3 --max-concurrency 4 --kv-capacity auto --kv-dtype int8 --max-context 131072. --max-concurrency was 8 here until 2026-08-27, when it was measured to segfault the server: a 99,878-token agent prompt (221 messages, tool history on) killed it during prefill inside bf16_gdn_gating_proj_kernels.cu with cudaErrorUnknown, container exit 139, taking every in-flight request with it. The same prompt from the same deployment completes in 56s at --max-concurrency 4, and an 84,915-token probe in 22s. Fewer slots also buy a bigger pool, not a smaller one: KV capacity auto resolves to 232,768 tokens at 4 against 187,712 at 8, because the per-slot workspace the gating kernel launches over is what the extra slots were costing. Over-length prompts are refused cleanly at 4 (context_length_exceeded at prepare), so the crash was never a context limit in disguise. The last two are load-bearing and were learned the expensive way on 2026-08-17: at --max-context 32768 a full-horizon descent run dies at round 13. NInfer rejects at `prepare` with a 400 rather than truncating, the harness records a turn that acted zero times, and the simulation advances anyway — so the run played out its remaining 130 turns with nobody in it and scored a clean zero. 32768 is ample for a 6-round cohort arm and nowhere near a 40-round run, which is why the smoke test passed. For scale: vLLM serves these same weights at --max-model-len 200000 over a 68,992-token KV cache, so any NInfer cap below ~128k is a regression against the server this target exists to be compared with. --kv-dtype int8 is what pays for it: it takes the KV pool from 96,768 to 187,712 tokens at --max-concurrency 8, and to 232,768 at 4 (measured, all from the server's own `KV capacity auto resolved` line), and the quality matrix of 2026-08-17 found no measurable difference against bf16 KV. vLLM makes the same trade with fp8_e4m3.
